messages:
lucas: Quick sync  we're blocking on policy compilation perf for the large tenant rollout. Current compile time ~120ms per policy change and we recompile often. Thoughts?

marie: 120ms isn't terrible but at scale it adds up if we invalidate caches frequently. Why are we recompiling on read?

dina: We do a shallow merge + compile for every tenant merge because overlay semantics were tricky. We can probably move compilation off the hot path.

raj: Proposal: incremental compiler that compiles only changed nodes in the policy AST and keeps a pluggable verifier stage. So overlay apply = merge delta -> patch AST -> recompile affected subgraph.

lucas: Sounds good. Do we have invariants that make incremental safe? e.g., penalty curves referencing global functions.

marie: Need to restrict cross-node references. If overlays are allowed only to set simple fields (region_preference, cost_multiplier) we can guarantee changes are local. Otherwise invalidation becomes global.

ops-bot: note: policy-linter v0.9 warns about cross-field refs in overlays.

raj: Implementation sketch:
```
- store core_policy AST precompiled in shared store
- overlays are parsed into delta ASTs (no global refs allowed)
- incremental compiler computes diff nodes and runs verification only on affected nodes
- cache merged compiled policy blob per-tenant with generation id
```

marie: We should also add a compatibility marker on compiled blobs: compiler-version + invariants-hash. That lets runtime reject incompatible blobs after a deploy.

dina: Good call. Runtime needs to detect "stale-compiler" at eval time and fallback to safe path (serve using core_policy only). We can't block requests during a rollout.

lucas: What about rollout ordering? If we deploy a compiler change, generated compiled policies might be unreadable by older runtimes. Sequence should be: 1) ship runtime that can ignore new marker and fall back; 2) deploy compiler and generate new blobs; 3) enable runtime read.

raj: Exactly. Migration plan: backward-compatible runtime -> compiler -> enable opt-in. Also add a feature-flag that lets us turn on incremental compile per-tenant. Start with 0.1% traffic.

marie: For verification we need unit tests plus simulation. Dina can you add a set of golden overlays that exercise edge-cases (region pin + cost bump + burst allowance) and run through policy-sim.

dina: Yup. I'll also add fuzz tests for AST merges to catch reference leaks.

ops-bot: telemetry: emit policy-compile-duration, policy-merge-count, policy-cache-hit.

lucas: Re caching: use generation ttl like 5m and invalidate on overlay update. But for high-churn tenants maybe shorter TTL. We should expose per-tenant TTL in admin UI.

raj: One more thing: debugging tools. We need a "policy-inspect" endpoint that returns merged YAML + compiled marker + provenance (which overlay caused the diff). Keep that output rate-limited and RBAC gated.

marie: Agree. Also provide a "preview" API that runs a dry-eval of a candidate overlay against a sample trace and returns metrics (p95, fallback-rate, cost-estimate). That helps SREs and support.

dina: Edge case: overlay referencing unavailable model variants. Validation should fail at submit time. Already catching that in model-catalog check but add unit test.

lucas: Risks: complexity of incremental compiler vs debugging overhead. If we ship it, we must have extensive logging and a rollback path to full compile.

raj: Action items:
- raj: prototype incremental patcher + generation id in compiler (WIP, due Tue)
- dina: golden overlays + fuzz merges + policy-sim integration (due Fri)
- marie: rollout sequencing doc + compat markers spec (due Thu)
- lucas: admin UI hooks for TTL + policy-inspect RBAC (due next Mon)

ops-bot: created taskboard: incremental-compiler prototyping -> policy-sim tests -> compatibility gating -> admin-ui.

marie: If we keep overlay allowed fields small this becomes much simpler. Let's finalize allowed fields list in RFC and then build the compiler.

lucas: Agreed. I'll open the RFC PR with the allowed-fields proposal and a note about incremental compile as an implementation option.

ops-bot: reminder: weekly architecture sync tomorrow to review prototype. :calendar: 

raj: cool. I'll follow up with a short demo once the patcher runs locally.
